images.title: Ten tenths make a unit
images.purpose: Show the regrouping step in 2 7/10 + 3 6/10: 7 tenths plus 6 tenths is 13 tenths, which is 1 unit and 3 tenths.
images.composition: Two strips stacked in the centre; the top strip is a full unit, the lower strip holds the leftover tenths, with an arrow between.
exact_structure: Top strip: one rectangle split into 10 equal cells, 7 teal (#0072B2) cells on the left and 3 amber (#E69F00) cells on the right, outlined with a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) border and labelled 1 unit.
Below it, a second strip of only 3 amber cells (3 cells wide, same cell size) labelled 3 tenths left.
A dashed grey (#6B7280) line links the lower strip to the top strip to show the 3 leftover tenths are the ones beyond a full unit.
Total amber cells are 6 (3 in the top strip and 3 in the lower strip) and teal cells are 7.
Left of the strips, a legend: a teal square labelled 7 tenths and an amber square labelled 6 tenths.
Beneath, one caption line: 7 + 6 = 13 tenths = 1 unit + 3 tenths.
rejection: total cells drawn is not 13 (10 in the top strip plus 3 below)
teal count not 7 or amber count not 6
the top strip does not have exactly 10 cells
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When tenths reach 10 they are regrouped into one unit.
images.description: A strip of ten cells with seven teal and three amber, and three more amber cells below, showing 13 tenths as 1 unit and 3 tenths.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the 13 cells and see that ten of them fill a unit.

image_decisions.why: The regrouping of 13 tenths is the new step in adding lengths in tenths, so it is the one thing drawn.
